newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: New Portuguese police chief pledges discipline.
newsitem.headline: New Portuguese police chief pledges discipline.

text.p: Portugal's new police chief Mario Goncalves Amaro pledged after being sworn in on Monday to tighten discipline within the force, shaken by charges of human rights abuses.
His predecessor General Gabriel Teixeira was fired last week by Interior Minister Alberto Costa in a row over the killing of a drug addict, shot in the back as he fled a robbery.

Teixeira angered the government by openly supporting the action of police in several Portuguese cities, who handed in their weapons for 24 hours over Christmas to protest against the detention of the officer who fired the fatal shot.
He was sacked after he failed to produce a plan requested by the government to improve discipline in the police, repeatedly accused in recent months of using excessive force.
"I will be intransigent and rigorous in matters of discipline and I will not accept attitudes harmful to the good name of the police," Amaro said at his swearing-in.
The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Antonio Guterres in a clear gesture of solidarity with Costa, who has been heavily criticised in the Portuguese press as being slow to act.
Police in the southern city of Evora, where the shooting took place just before Christmas, initially announced that the youth had died after being taken ill.
In November, the European Committee against Torture accused Portuguese police of frequently mistreating people in custody, saying the most common abuse was blows inflicted with fists or clubs.
